title: Subquadratic-space 3SUM indexing with polylogarithmic queries
formal: Do there exist constants \(\delta>0\) and \(C\ge1\) and uniform randomized preprocessing and query algorithms such that, for every \(n\ge2\) and \(A,B\subseteq\{0,\ldots,n^4-1\}\) with \(|A|=|B|=n\), the resulting static index uses at most \(O(n^{2-\delta})\) words and answers whether \(z\in A+B\) in \(O((\log n)^C)\) worst-case time? Each fixed query must be correct with probability at least \(2/3\).
definitions: A uniform sequential word RAM has a fixed finite program, word-sized registers and addressed memory cells. Unit-cost instructions are reads and writes, comparisons, branching, addition, subtraction, multiplication, integer division with nonzero divisor, Boolean bit operations and logical shifts. Arithmetic stored in one word is modulo \(2^w\); shifts by at least \(w\) yield zero. Addresses must fit the available word size. All table construction and input-dependent auxiliary memory count; there is no free advice or input-dependent oracle. Randomized programs may generate independent uniform random words. Use \(w=\lceil10\log_2(n+2)\rceil\)-bit words. A query is \(z\in\{0,\ldots,2n^4-2\}\), and \(A+B=\{a+b:a\in A,b\in B\}\) uses ordinary integer addition without wraparound. Preprocessing time is unrestricted but must terminate almost surely; its resulting representation must always respect the space budget. Randomized queries use fresh internal randomness, and the per-query success probability is over both preprocessing and query randomness for every fixed \((A,B,z)\). Queries read a static representation and cannot carry free input-dependent information across calls. All stored inputs, hash seeds and auxiliary tables count toward space. The constants and programs must be independent of the input and \(n\). A polynomial universe with exponent four avoids the small-universe direct-address case; it is an explicit benchmark regime of the broader indexing question.
why: This asks whether a quadratic family of potential sums can support fast membership queries without a nearly quadratic representation.

context_blocks.text: The original space-hardness framework distinguishes a polylogarithmic-query conjecture from the stronger conjecture allowing polynomially slower queries. The stronger version has been refuted.
The later time-space improvements do not establish truly subquadratic space with polylogarithmic queries. The card asks for that remaining algorithmic possibility, allowing bounded error explicitly.

answer_criterion: Give a complete Lean-checked proof of the stated existence claim or its logical negation, with the same inputs, computation model, space allowance, quantifiers and cost guarantees. A result for a restricted input family or a different model does not decide the full target.

notes: Fixes a polynomial integer universe and bounded-error word-RAM convention. This is the positive algorithmic question from the discussion, not the already-refuted strong 3SUM-indexing conjecture.

category_assignment.reason: The question is about static representation size and query time after preprocessing, distinct from solving one 3SUM instance.

sentences: Two sets of integers are preprocessed once.
Each query asks whether a supplied number is a sum of one element from each set.
Storing all sums uses quadratic space and permits fast lookup.
The question asks for a polynomial saving in space while keeping polylogarithmic queries.
Older stronger tradeoff conjectures are distinguished from this remaining target.
